title: Cutover failures can bypass the promised report
description: The module docstring at `scripts/cutover_227_tick_backup.py:2-8` promises that the first failure stops the run and the report is still written. But `run_steps()` at lines 269-284 only catches `StepFailed` and `subprocess.CalledProcessError`, while `main()` at lines 287-316 writes the report only after `run_steps()` returns. Ordinary operational failures raise other exceptions and skip `report.write_text()` at line 312: `CRON_FILE.read_text()` at line 95 and `tick_commands()` at `scripts/cutover_227_host.py:99-100` can raise `FileNotFoundError`; `step_production()` at `scripts/cutover_227_tick_backup.py:224` can raise `FileNotFoundError` or `IndexError` on a missing/empty health log; `conf_sums()` at `scripts/cutover_227_host.py:81-82` can raise `StopIteration`; and `int(psql(...))` at `scripts/cutover_227_host.py:96` can raise `ValueError`. Add a documented top-level handler or `try/finally` around report writing, record the exception/traceback in `step.seen`, and still emit the FAIL report.

title: Lock query builds SQL with constants instead of parameterized values
description: `tick_locks_held()` at lines 90-96 builds `objid IN ({keys})` with an f-string and sends the resulting SQL to `psql()` at `scripts/cutover_227_host.py:59-62` as a literal `-c` argument. The SQL rules require parameterized queries and prefer `EXISTS` over `COUNT` for existence checks. Even though `TICK_LOCK_KEYS` are trusted integer constants, this is string-built SQL and should not be the pattern for a database-facing host primitive. Use `SELECT EXISTS(...)` with bound/quoted values via a parameterized client or psql variables, and return a boolean rather than counting all matching locks.

title: Offsite verification discards push command failures and output
description: `step_offsite()` at lines 207-217 calls `shell(tick_commands()["push"], step)` at line 209 but ignores the returned `CompletedProcess`. `shell()` at `scripts/cutover_227_host.py:53-56` captures stdout/stderr but only appends the command text to `step.seen`; no `record()` call is made. If `sync_wal_offsite.sh` exits non-zero, the cutover report contains neither its exit code nor its error output, and the step can still pass if the later `rclone check` calls are clean. The same observability gap appears in `step_weekly()` at `scripts/cutover_227_tick_backup.py:173-187` and `step_metadata()` at lines 192-195, which rely on log tails and return codes but do not record stdout/stderr for failures before log redirection. Record each shell result and explicitly assert the push command’s success, or document and handle an allowed skip.

title: `--check --rehearse` creates a directory despite the no-change contract
description: The header comment at `deploy/setup-backup.sh:4-8` says `--check` changes nothing, but the rehearsal setup at lines 134-138 runs `mkdir -p "$REHEARSE"` whenever `--rehearse` is supplied, including check mode, before step 1. The tests in `test/unit/test_setup_backup.py` invoke `_check(host)` with `--rehearse` and assert that no `cron.d` or cluster directories are created, but a normal check still leaves `$REHEARSE` behind; `test_malformed_table_stops_before_any_step` only sees no rehearsal directory because table parsing happens before this block. Create the rehearsal root only in apply mode, require the caller to create it, or update the documented `--check` contract and tests to state this side effect explicitly.

title: Production cron comparison hard-codes the table's replication host
description: `strip_new_args()` at lines 84-88 removes ` --replication-host 127.0.0.1` using a literal, while `production_changes()` at lines 91-99 accepts only `url_key` and `bucket_remote`; `step_apply()` at `scripts/cutover_227_tick_backup.py:114-116` likewise passes only those two values. The `17/main` row in `deploy/backup-clusters.conf` defines the replication host, and `test/unit/test_setup_backup.py` repeats the same literal in `_NEW_MAIN_ARGS`. This scatters one comparison value across config, helper, cutover call, and test. If the table’s replication host changes, the TD3 comparison can fail even though the rendered cron is correct. Pass `ctx.main.replication_host` into the comparison and derive the test’s expected arguments from the same table/parser.

title: New provisioning tests assert source text rather than behavior
description: The new 227 TD5 tests at `test/unit/test_provision_tick_lib.py:176-259` largely parse the shell script and SQL file as text: `test_only_trading_tick_is_created`, `test_parent_directories_755_data_directory_700`, `test_roles_are_applied_with_replication`, and `test_roles_sql_grants_replication_only_when_asked` assert exact assignment strings or substring ordering. This violates the testing rule against asserting implementation rather than behavior: harmless refactors can fail, while a behavioral regression that preserves a matching substring can pass. Prefer executing `hba_content()`/`ensure_databases()` through stubbed `tick_psql` that records arguments and outputs, or an integration fixture against a throwaway database, then assert generated HBA lines, invoked psql variables, and role attributes.

title: Health gate can accept a stale successful result
description: `run_health` ignores the return code from the health command and accepts the last `FLAGS` line in the log without verifying that this invocation wrote it. If the command fails before appending to the log, an earlier healthy result can satisfy the gate and allow later cutover steps to proceed. Check the command result and ensure the parsed log entry is fresh before treating the health check as successful.

title: Unexpected step errors bypass the cutover report
description: `run_steps` catches only `StepFailed` and `CalledProcessError`. Other operational errors—such as `FileNotFoundError` from a missing command or `OSError` from a log read—escape the loop, so `main` never writes the report despite the script’s stated guarantee that failures are recorded. Convert expected host-operation errors into a recorded step failure, or ensure report writing occurs even when an unexpected step error escapes.

title: Cutover script's "report is always written" guarantee does not hold for unchecked exceptions
`strip_new_args` hardcodes the replication host, duplicating the cluster table
description: `strip_new_args` removes the literal `" --replication-host 127.0.0.1"`. The same value is the `replication_host` column of `deploy/backup-clusters.conf:21` and is already parsed into `ctx.main.replication_host` (`scripts/backup_clusters.py`, `BackupCluster.replication_host`), yet `step_apply` passes only `ctx.main.url_key` and `ctx.bucket_remote` into `production_changes`. AGENTS.md is explicit here: "Never scatter comparison values across code. If a value is used in conditionals, switch cases, or lookups, define it once … and reference that definition everywhere." Because this is the comparison that protects production's schedule (TD3), a table edit to `replication_host` would silently stop the check from recognising the argument 227 adds, and the test that asserts the pre-227 equivalence would keep passing against its own hardcoded copy. Pass the row's host through from `ctx.main` instead.
